commitResults.messageTitle: Add tests for add, get, size and getAll
Add more tests, for Parser, Task, and Command
first stage of UI, from tutorial part 2
Add assert statements to document internal invariants
commitResults.messageBody:
Documents programmer assumptions that should always hold internally,
  as distinct from user-input validation (which stays exception-based
  since asserts are compiled out by default):

  - Command#toValidIndex: the index it returns is always in range once
    the range check above it passes.
  - Storage#parseLine: task is always assigned once the type switch
    falls through, since every case either assigns it or returns null.
  - Deadline/Event constructors: the date fields are always non-null
    (unlike the optional time fields), since both call sites (Parser,
    Storage) only reach these constructors after DateTimeUtil#parse has
    already succeeded.
  - DateTimeUtil#formatForDisplay/formatForSave: mirror the same
    required-date contract as the constructors above.
  - MainWindow#initialize and DialogBox's constructor: FXML-injected
    @FXML fields are non-null, since a renamed fx:id would otherwise
    only surface later as an unexplained NullPointerException.

  Considered adding similar bounds-check asserts to TaskList#get/remove,
  but TaskListTest exercises those methods directly with invalid
  indices expecting IndexOutOfBoundsException, so that would have
  asserted a caller-always-validates assumption the tests show isn't
  actually part of TaskList's contract.

  Verified with `./gradlew build` (tests, checkstyle, javadoc all pass).
  Assertions are disabled by default, so this doesn't change observable
  behavior; run with `-ea` (or via `./gradlew test`, which enables
  assertions by default) to have them active.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract duplicated startup-loading logic into Storage#loadOrEmpty
commitResults.messageBody:
The CLI entry point (MaggiGorengAyam.main) and the GUI entry point
(MaggiGorengAyamBot's constructor) each independently implemented the
same "load tasks, catch a hard IOException by falling back to an
empty list, and build a one-time warning message for skipped lines or
a load failure" sequence. The two copies only differed in where the
resulting message went (printed immediately vs. stored as a string
for later), everything else was identical.

Per the SE-EDU code quality guidelines
(https://nus-cs2103-ay2627-s1.github.io/website/se-book-adapted/chapters/codeQuality.html),
this is exactly the kind of duplication worth removing: the two
places have to be kept in sync by hand, and it's easy to lose track
of that when they live in different files and packages. Reviewed the
rest of the codebase against the same guidelines (method length,
nesting, magic numbers, naming, comments) and didn't find anything
else at this severity - everything else already follows the
guidelines reasonably closely.

Fix: added Storage#loadOrEmpty(Ui), which performs the load, catches
the IOException, and returns a new Storage.StartupResult bundling the
resulting TaskList with a nullable message (built via the Ui methods
that already existed for this purpose: showLoadWarning/
showLoadingError). Both entry points now call this one method and
just decide how to surface the message, removing ~12 duplicated lines
per call site.

This does add a Storage -> Ui dependency that didn't exist before.
Considered keeping Storage UI-agnostic and only extracting the
try/catch/unwrapping part, but that would have left the "which
message to show" branching duplicated too, which is the more
error-prone half of the original duplication. Given Ui already
depends on TaskList/Task (the domain types), and showLoadWarning/
showLoadingError exist for no other purpose than this call site, the
added coupling seemed like a reasonable, well-contained trade-off
for a small student project rather than introducing a new class
solely to avoid it.

Verified with `./gradlew build` (compiles, checkstyle, javadoc, and
all existing unit tests pass) plus a manual run of the CLI against
TC1/TC2 from test/ui-test-plan.md and the empty-file/successful-load/
skipped-line-warning paths in Storage#loadOrEmpty directly - console
output is byte-for-byte unchanged, so no update to
test/ui-test-plan.md was needed.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use Java Streams for list filtering and building
commitResults.messageBody:
Replaces manual for-loops with Streams pipelines wherever the loop was
a plain filter/map/collect - imperative index/counter bookkeeping that
Streams expresses more directly:

- FindCommand/OnCommand: the for-loop + if + ArrayList.add() pattern
  for filtering tasks becomes tasks.getAll().stream().filter(...)
  .collect(Collectors.toList()).
- Ui: showTaskList/showTasksOn/showMatchingTasks each had their own
  near-identical StringBuilder loop for numbering tasks from 1.
  Extracted into one numberedLines(List<Task>) helper built with
  IntStream.range(0, size).mapToObj(...).collect(Collectors.joining())
  - needs IntStream rather than a plain object stream since the
  1-based number comes from the index, not the element.
- Storage#load: the loop built a task list while also counting
  skipped lines via a mutable counter. Replaced with one pipeline that
  maps each line to a parsed Task (or null) and then
  Collectors.partitioningBy(Objects::isNull) splits the results into
  parsed and skipped in a single pass, with no counter variable.
- Storage#save: tasks.stream().map(task -> task.toSaveFormat() +
  System.lineSeparator()).collect(Collectors.joining()) builds the
  file content in one expression instead of a manual write-loop.

Left Storage#parseLine as a plain switch: its type-dispatch with
early returns and per-branch exception handling doesn't map cleanly
onto a stream pipeline, and forcing it into one would hurt readability
rather than help it.

Verified with `./gradlew build` (compiles, checkstyle, javadoc, and
all unit tests pass), plus manual runs covering every changed path:
list/find/on numbering, a save-then-reload round trip, the
skipped-line load-warning, and saving an empty task list (confirms
Collectors.joining() with no tasks still produces a 0-byte file,
matching the original loop's behavior). Console output is
byte-for-byte unchanged, so no test/ui-test-plan.md update was needed.
